issue.title: Internal mypy error (failed `assert supertype is not None`) on parametrized class
issue.body:
I'm playing around with computable unbound sets, i.e. `{1,2,3,...}` (in which `...` is not `Ellipsis`, but 'etc.') and its kin.
On the latest `PyPI` version (0.961), I get 
```
<source>.py:40: error: INTERNAL ERROR -- Please try using mypy master on GitHub:
https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/common_issues.html#using-a-development-mypy-build
If this issue continues with mypy master, please report a bug at https://github.com/python/mypy/issues
version: 0.961
discours1.py:40: : note: please use --show-traceback to print a traceback when reporting a bug
```
source file gist URL: https://gist.github.com/0b2320a6eb6223687f490feadb263d2d

The same happens on master, playground URL: https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=master&python=3.10&flags=show-traceback&gist=0b2320a6eb6223687f490feadb263d2d

**WITHOUT** the `test()` function (so just definition, not use of `ComputedSet`), `mypy` reports clean (also in `--strict`). **WITH** instantation of `ComputedSet[...](...)`, `mypy` stops with error.

issue.title: Fix crashes on special forms in protocol bodies
issue.body:
Fixes #6801
Fixes #10577
Fixes #12642
Fixes #12337
Fixes #10639 
Fixes #13390 

All these crashes are in a sense duplicates of each other. Fix is trivial, except I decided to ban type aliases in protocol bodies. Already in the examples in issues, I have found two cases where people wrote `foo = list[str]`, where they clearly wanted `foo: list[str]`. This can cause hard to spot false negatives.
